hero.name: Anna Burgess
hero.headline: Mechanical design, manufacturing, robotics, propulsion, controls, and hands-on engineering.
hero.intro: I’m a Mechanical Engineering student at Harvard focused on taking systems from analysis and CAD through machining, assembly, testing, and iteration. My work spans liquid rocketry, robotics, computational mechanics, controls, research hardware, manufacturing, and personal fabrication.

about.title: Engineering from first principles to hardware.
paragraphs: I am pursuing a B.S. in Mechanical Engineering at Harvard College with a minor in Mathematical Sciences. My coursework includes computer-aided machine design, mechanical systems, solid and computational mechanics, and robotics.

My experience is strongly fabrication-driven: manual and CNC machining, welding, 3D printing, laser and waterjet cutting, soldering, CAD/CAE, embedded controls, fixture design, testing, and iterative build work.
Outside coursework, I lead and contribute to rocketry and robotics programs, work in research environments, and build personal projects ranging from CNC equipment to vehicle restoration.

fud.title: Forward Unto Dawn — Regeneratively Cooled Liquid Bipropellant Engine
fud.summary: Liquid bipropellant engine development centered on regenerative cooling, an additively manufactured combustion chamber, and analytical validation.
fud.desc: Development of a liquid bipropellant, regeneratively cooled rocket engine with a metal additively manufactured combustion chamber. The project combines propulsion analysis, mechanical design, manufacturing constraints, assembly, and test planning.
fud.contrib: Led and contributed to the engineering effort across design coordination, hardware development, propulsion analysis, and integration. Analytical work included validation using NASA CEA tools.

rocketlink.title: RocketLink Telemetry System
rocketlink.summary: Long-range LoRa/GPS telemetry project with custom avionics housings for flight hardware.
rocketlink.desc: A telemetry system intended to provide long-range communication and position data for rocket flight operations using LoRa and GPS hardware.
rocketlink.contrib: Personally designed the housings for the electronics system and supported integration and flight-test preparation.

sphinx.title: Mojave Sphinx Rocket + Static Test Stand
sphinx.summary: Rocket assembly, component manufacturing, and development of a dedicated engine static-test stand.
sphinx.desc: A hardware-intensive rocketry effort spanning test infrastructure, rocket component manufacturing, vehicle assembly, and static-fire operations.
sphinx.contrib: Designed, built, and installed the test stand at the team site; manufactured Sphinx components; led and completed a significant portion of vehicle assembly; supported static-fire operations.

irec.title: IREC 10K COTS Competition Rocket
irec.summary: Active development of a 10,000-ft COTS competition rocket for IREC.
irec.desc: An active student-led effort to develop a 10,000-ft COTS competition rocket for IREC, building the team capability, technical architecture, and project organization required to take the vehicle from concept through flight readiness.
irec.contrib: Founded the 10,000-ft IREC program and began organizing the engineering team, technical workstreams, schedule, and certification pipeline.

l1.title: NAR Level 1 High-Power Rocketry Certification
l1.summary: Built and launched an Apogee Zephyr to successfully earn NAR Level 1 certification.
l1.desc: A high-power rocketry certification project involving construction, inspection, launch preparation, flight, and recovery of an Apogee Zephyr rocket.
l1.contrib: Built the rocket, completed launch preparation, flew and recovered the vehicle successfully, and earned NAR Level 1 High Power Rocketry certification.

phase1.title: Phase 1 Liquid Bipropellant Rocket Design
phase1.summary: Early-stage liquid bipropellant vehicle design including bulkhead FEA, concept sketches, and structural geometry optimization.
phase1.desc: An early-phase liquid bipropellant rocket concept that explored vehicle structure, bulkhead load paths, and packaging before the program was indefinitely suspended.
phase1.contrib: Performed SolidWorks FEA on bulkheads, developed concept sketches, and used material cutaways and geometry iteration to optimize bulkhead designs.

urc.title: University Rover Challenge — Rover Manufacturing
urc.summary: Precision manufacturing for a Mars rover, including suspension and arm power-transmission hardware.
urc.desc: Manufacturing and DFM work for a University Rover Challenge Mars rover with custom mechanical subsystems across the suspension, arm, chassis, and science hardware.
urc.contrib: Personally manufactured approximately 90% of the rover’s machined components, including power-transmission components in the suspension and arm. Selected manufacturing approaches and redesigned parts to reduce setup complexity.

ability.title: Servo-Driven Visual Perturbation Headset
ability.summary: Low-cost experimental headset using servo-driven mirrors to induce controlled balance perturbations.
ability.desc: A research hardware platform designed to alter a participant’s visual field through controlled mirror motion so balance responses could be studied during data collection.
ability.contrib: Designed and fabricated the low-cost headset and integrated servo-driven mirrors for controlled experimental perturbations.

mahi.title: Force-Sensing Wearable Hardware
mahi.summary: Equation-driven CAD and 3D-printed housings for force-sensitive resistors used in wearable sensing applications.
mahi.desc: Research focused on force-sensitive resistor integration for a center-of-pressure sensing insole and a force-quantifying scoliosis brace. Designs were iterated through CAD, additive manufacturing, and experimental validation.
mahi.contrib: Designed FSR housings using equation-driven SolidWorks models, iterated parts through 3D printing, and validated sensor behavior with Instron testing. Presented the work at the Rice Summer Undergraduate Research Symposium.

yellow.title: Yellow Jacket Competition Robot
yellow.summary: Competition robot that collected tennis balls, placed them on a Velcro wall, and climbed 15° and 30° inclines.
yellow.desc: A semester-long machine-design competition project requiring a robot to collect tennis balls, transport and place them on a Velcro scoring wall, and negotiate multiple inclines.
yellow.contrib: Contributed to mechanical design, CAD, fabrication, assembly, troubleshooting, and competition preparation.

nerf.title: Red Light–Green Light Nerf Turret
nerf.summary: Squid Game-inspired motion-responsive Nerf turret using PIR sensors.
nerf.desc: A mechatronics final project inspired by the red light–green light game in Squid Game. PIR motion sensing was used to detect movement and drive the system behavior.
nerf.contrib: Contributed to concept development, sensor integration, mechanical/electrical implementation, and final system demonstration.

bridge.title: Optimized I-Beam Bridge
bridge.summary: Wood bridge optimized for compression force-to-weight performance and tested in an Instron.
bridge.desc: A structural optimization project where wood bridges were evaluated by maximum force resisted before deformation divided by bridge weight.
bridge.contrib: Helped optimize cross-sectional geometry around an I-beam-inspired design, fabricated the structure, and prepared it for Instron compression testing.

egg.title: Variable-Damping Egg Drop System
egg.summary: Spring-damper protection system using shaped tracks to vary damping behavior through compression.
egg.desc: An impact-mitigation system designed around springs and dampers. The damper geometry was varied throughout compression so the effective damping response changed through the stroke to reduce peak egg acceleration.
egg.contrib: Developed and implemented the mechanically varying damping concept using mathematically driven track curves and contributed to system design, fabrication, and testing.

abaqus.title: Parametric Abaqus Unit-Cell Compression Model
abaqus.summary: Python-driven Abaqus model varying side count, radius, and height to study compression response.
abaqus.desc: A parametric finite-element workflow for studying how geometric parameters affect a unit cell under compression. Geometry generation and analysis were automated to enable systematic comparison.
abaqus.contrib: Built the Python-based parametric Abaqus workflow and enabled variation of number of sides, radius, and height for comparative analysis.

controls.title: Friction & Backlash Compensation Test Platform
controls.summary: Controlled test setup for varying friction and backlash and developing a PID controller with compensation.
controls.desc: A controls platform designed to introduce known, adjustable amounts of friction and backlash so their impact on system response could be measured experimentally.
controls.contrib: Designed the experimental setup, gathered response data under controlled variation, and developed a PID controller incorporating friction and backlash compensation.

plasma.title: 3-Axis CNC Plasma Cutter
plasma.summary: Arduino/GRBL-controlled 3-axis CNC plasma system with NEMA motors and a removable commercial torch.
plasma.desc: A custom CNC plasma cutting platform designed around a removable off-the-shelf plasma torch so the torch can be used both within and independently of the CNC system.
plasma.contrib: Designed the mechanical housing and motion system, integrated NEMA motors and Arduino/GRBL controls, and designed a removable torch mount.

vehicles.title: Vehicle Restoration & Repair
vehicles.summary: Electrical, ignition, transmission, and engine work across a 1969 Ford F-350 and 1973 El Camino.
vehicles.desc: Ongoing restoration and troubleshooting work spanning electrical systems, ignition, drivetrain service, and engine restoration on older vehicles.
vehicles.contrib: Completed a full wiring-harness redo on a 1969 Ford F-350; independently diagnosed distributor and ignition-module issues on a 1973 El Camino; performed transmission removal and repair; and worked on restoration of a 400 small-block Chevrolet engine.

textiles.title: Crochet & Sewing
textiles.summary: Textile projects exploring patterning, construction methods, materials, and hands-on fabrication.
textiles.desc: A collection of crochet and sewing projects extending my interest in making and fabrication into flexible materials and textile construction.
textiles.contrib: Design, pattern interpretation, material selection, sewing, crochet, finishing, and iteration across personal projects.

stocksmart.title: StockSmart — Wyss Institute Storage Solution
stocksmart.summary: A new storage solution designed for the Wyss Institute at Harvard to address problems caused by disproportionate billing.
stocksmart.desc: StockSmart was a semester-long design project developed for the Wyss Institute at Harvard. The project focused on redesigning how materials or supplies were stored and managed in response to problems the institute was experiencing with disproportionate billing. The team worked through the design process from problem definition and stakeholder needs to concept development and a final proposed storage solution.
stocksmart.contrib: Contributed to the semester-long engineering design process, including understanding the client problem, developing and evaluating concepts, refining the storage-system design, and preparing the final technical documentation and presentation.
stocksmart.result: Semester-long class design project for the Wyss Institute at Harvard

square-pendulum.title: Square Pendulum Normal Modes
square-pendulum.summary: Experimental study of a square pendulum system to identify and characterize its normal modes.
square-pendulum.desc: A wave-phenomena class project centered on a square pendulum. The project investigated the coupled motion of the system and worked to identify the distinct normal modes that govern its behavior.
square-pendulum.contrib: Contributed to building and testing the square-pendulum setup, collecting observations and measurements, analyzing the system response, and identifying the normal modes for the final presentation.

heat-transfer.title: Infrared Imaging as an Indicator of Plant Drought Stress
heat-transfer.summary: Two-week experiment using six fern plants, controlled watering levels, and daily IR imaging to investigate whether thermal imagery can reveal drought stress before plant death.
heat-transfer.desc: My partner and I conducted a two-week heat-transfer experiment using six fern plants that received different amounts of water. We captured infrared images of the plants each day and compared their thermal behavior over time to investigate whether IR imaging could serve as an early indicator of drought stress before visible decline or plant death.
heat-transfer.contrib: Co-designed and conducted the experiment, maintained the different watering conditions, collected daily infrared images for two weeks, and analyzed the resulting temperature patterns to evaluate whether thermal imaging could indicate drought stress early.

senior-thesis.contrib: This is my senior thesis / capstone project, so I will use this space to document my individual technical ownership, design decisions, analysis, fabrication, testing, and iteration as the work progresses.

engineering-music.title: Instrument Design & Fabrication
engineering-music.summary: A hands-on course project centered on designing and building musical instruments while connecting engineering principles with sound and music.
engineering-music.desc: For my Engineering and Music GenEd, I designed and built physical musical instruments as part of a hands-on exploration of how engineering choices shape sound. The project connected design and fabrication with the physical behavior that produces musical tones.
engineering-music.contrib: Designed and fabricated the instruments, iterated on the physical design, and applied engineering reasoning to connect geometry, construction, and material choices with the resulting acoustic behavior.
engineering-music.result: Course project · instrument design and fabrication
